basic_info.name: Nuance DAX Copilot (rebranded Microsoft Dragon Copilot)
basic_info.description: Microsoft's ambient clinical documentation assistant (formerly Nuance Dragon Ambient eXperience, now folded into Dragon Copilot after the March 2025 merger with Dragon Medical One) that listens to a live clinician-patient encounter and drafts structured clinical notes inside the EHR. The single most load-bearing fact is its position: it is the doctor-side, during-encounter incumbent with the largest install base (Microsoft cites 100,000+ clinicians across 600+ organizations) and the deepest bidirectional Epic FHIR write-back in the category. It does not capture patient-elicited pre-visit history, does not emit an interoperable FHIR document (it writes note text and discrete fields into the EHR), and runs cloud-only on Microsoft Azure.
basic_info.organization: Microsoft Corporation (product originated at Nuance Communications, acquired by Microsoft in 2022)

technical_features.what_it_does: Captures a live clinician-patient conversation via mobile, web or desktop app (or embedded in Epic), transcribes and diarizes speakers with Dragon speech recognition, and uses an LLM to draft specialty-aware note sections - history of present illness (HPI), review of systems (ROS), physical exam (PE), and assessment & plan (A&P) - that the clinician reviews, edits and signs before it is written back into the EHR. It also produces referral letters, after-visit summaries, order suggestions within Epic, and (from 2026) diagnosis-aware notes and ICD-10 coding suggestions. It does not elicit a patient history before the encounter and does not emit a standards-based summary document such as an NRCeS/AYUSH OPConsultRecord Composition.
technical_features.architecture: Cloud-only SaaS built on Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare. Combines Nuance Dragon Medical One speech recognition with generative LLM note drafting ('ambient' layer), a generative clinical assistant, and Dragon Copilot desktop/web/mobile clients. Integrates with EHRs through the Dragon Copilot integration service using HL7 SMART App Launch (v2.x) and FHIR R4, and by enabling a limited set of Epic FHIR APIs (AllergyIntolerance, DocumentReference, MedicationRequest/MedicationDispense, etc.) to ground output in authoritative chart data. Regional integration endpoints per country (US, Canada, France, Germany, UK).
technical_features.inputs: Live encounter audio (in-room, telehealth or hybrid) with multi-speaker capture; EHR structured and unstructured context pulled via FHIR - medications, conditions, allergies, prior notes, document references, practitioner/location directories, vitals and problem lists. No patient-facing pre-visit questionnaire or document upload path (no file upload / PDF ingestion).
technical_features.outputs: Draft clinical note text in clinician-specified structured sections (HPI, ROS, PE, A&P; SOAP/APSO/H&P/progress variants), referral letters, after-visit summaries, order suggestions, and ICD-10 code suggestions (2026). Output is transferred into the EHR note editor and discrete fields - not a portable FHIR Bundle/Composition document. There is no exposed structured-summary artifact for downstream FHIR exchange.
technical_features.standards_compliance: Claims/validated use of HL7 SMART App Launch Framework v2.x and FHIR R4 for EHR launch and context (validated in Microsoft Learn SDK documentation), with FHIR API activation for specific Epic resources including AllergyIntolerance, Binary, DocumentReference, Location, MedicationDispense, MedicationRequest and PractitionerRole (all R4). It does not claim or validate conformance to NRCeS NDHM/ABDM Implementation Guide profiles (OPConsultRecord, HealthDocumentRecord), nor to HL7 IPS, SNOMED CT or LOINC as an emitted document. Compliance posture is privacy/security focused - HIPAA BAA through Microsoft Azure, HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type II / SOC 3 - which is orthogonal to clinical FHIR document conformance. Note: it is reported as not PIPEDA-compliant for Canada.
technical_features.offline_capability: None. Cloud-only: audio is processed server-side in Azure, and the product requires connectivity for capture, inference and EHR write-back. No local storage, no store-and-forward, no on-device inference mode. Recordings are retained (reportedly up to 30 days) for processing/QA. This is the opposite of the offline-first posture MediKiosk requires.
technical_features.languages_supported: English and Spanish natively. An admin-enabled 'Multilingual' recording mode adds 50+ additional languages (58 languages cited at HIMSS 2026), including Hindi, but the clinician must manually select the language before recording, it cannot be changed mid-session, and Microsoft's own documentation warns accuracy 'might not be as accurate' and that notes are always generated in English. Voice commands are English-only. There is no Devanagari output and no support for code-mixed Hinglish; non-selected multilingual speech is read phonetically as English.
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud (Microsoft Azure); accessed through EHR-embedded app, web browser, desktop application, and mobile app (iOS and Android as of the 2025 Dragon Copilot rebrand; the original DAX was iPhone-only). Enterprise-only procurement with IT/security deployment; targeted data residency in US, Canada, UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands and Switzerland. No India region and no on-premise or kiosk deployment.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: A peer-reviewed evaluation scored DAX-generated notes 46.91 out of 50 for accuracy and completeness [uncertain - repeated by review sites but primary source not independently located]. Microsoft cites roughly 7 minutes saved per encounter and 99%+ speech recognition accuracy from the Dragon Medical One base. Independent peer-reviewed results are more sobering: the NEJM AI Atrium Health longitudinal study (112 DAX clinicians vs 103 controls, 180 days) found no statistically significant improvement in EHR or financial metrics overall, with exploratory reductions in documentation hours only for high users (mean ratio 0.93) and low-volume/family-medicine subgroups; the authors concluded widespread implementation was 'unlikely to generate appreciable gains' for productivity. The Stanford JAMIA pilot (45 physicians, 9,629/17,428 encounters, 55.25% utilization) found a median reduction of 0.57 minutes per note and 6.89 minutes/day of documentation. Qualitative failure mode repeatedly reported: the assessment-and-plan section is verbose 'fluff' requiring trimming, MDM synthesis is weak in high-acuity specialties, and quality varies in behavioral health. No standalone hallucination rate is published.
performance_metrics.latency: Real-time draft during the encounter; no precise time-to-note figure is published. [uncertain]
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: No local compute requirements - all inference is server-side on Azure; the client needs only a microphone-bearing device (iPhone, Android, desktop, or Epic Haiku/Rover). Exact RAM/VRAM/model-size disclosures are not published. [uncertain]
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: 100,000+ clinicians across 600+ healthcare organizations (Microsoft-cited, 2026); 200+ EHR footprint inherited from Dragon Medical One; 100+ supported specialties widely cited. Vendor survey reported 70% of clinicians reporting less burnout.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Mixed evidence base: peer-reviewed independent studies (NEJM AI longitudinal nonrandomized study NCT06329427; JAMA Network Open nonrandomized clinical trial; JAMIA prospective QI study at Stanford; Haberle et al. peer-matched controlled cohort) alongside vendor-commissioned claims (Microsoft's ~7 min/encounter, 70% burnout survey, 46.91/50 score). Notably, the most rigorous trial was not vendor-funded and found no group-level efficiency gain, while positive figures are largely vendor-reported. As of mid-2026 the indexed PubMed literature on DAX was reported as thin relative to its adoption scale. No published concept-recall, ROUGE, BERTScore or hallucination evaluation.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: DAX Copilot is the dominant deployed prior art for turning clinical conversation into structured notes, and it validates at scale that speech-to-structured-note generation is clinically usable and commercially accepted. For Module C it serves three purposes: (1) it proves the core capability (HPI/ROS/PE/A&P generation with clinician review) is real, setting an implicit quality bar; (2) it demonstrates the exact architecture MediKiosk must NOT copy - doctor-side, during-encounter, cloud-only, English/Spanish-centric, note-text-only, no pre-visit elicitation, no FHIR document emission; and (3) its independent evaluations supply the cautionary template for Module C's eval harness: group-level time savings are weak, quality is specialty-dependent, and vendor accuracy claims must be separated from peer-reviewed results. It does not compete with MediKiosk's pre-consultation, patient-facing, offline, NRCeS-conformant gap.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (a) section-structured note generation (HPI/ROS/PE/A&P) rather than a monolithic blob, which maps cleanly onto OPConsultRecord sections; (b) the mandatory clinician-review-and-signoff gate before content becomes authoritative - directly compatible with MediKiosk's physician attestation constraint; (c) grounding output in authoritative structured chart data rather than model inference alone, which for MediKiosk means grounding in Module A slots and Module B FHIR extracts with per-field provenance; (d) specialty/context-tuned templates rather than one generic SOAP shell. Reject: (a) cloud-only inference - MediKiosk is offline-first; (b) English/Spanish native with a manual multilingual toggle - MediKiosk requires bilingual Hindi/Devanagari and Hinglish by design; (c) note-text-only output - Module C must emit a validated NRCeS OPConsultRecord Bundle, not paste text into a chart; (d) enterprise-only procurement and per-provider licensing as a product model; (e) evaluation that never isolates hallucination/omission.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Persistent editing burden - verbose A&P 'fluff' and weak medical decision-making synthesis force clinicians to revise notes, eroding claimed time savings. Evidence gap: the most rigorous trial found no group-level efficiency benefit and there is no published hallucination rate. Language limitations: native English/Spanish only; multilingual mode requires manual selection, cannot switch mid-session, generates English notes, and is explicitly warned as less accurate. No offline/edge capability and no India data-residency region. No pre-visit patient history elicitation and no document (PDF/image) upload or OCR. No standalone interoperable FHIR summary document - value is locked into EHR-native write-back. Procurement requires enterprise sales, setup fees and 3-6 month deployment. It is also reported as not PIPEDA-compliant, limiting Canadian use.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: The architectures are nearly orthogonal. DAX is doctor-side and during-encounter; MediKiosk is patient-facing and pre-consultation. DAX is cloud-only Azure with a microphone; MediKiosk is offline-first on a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk. DAX natively handles English/Spanish and bolsters 58 languages only manually; MediKiosk requires bilingual Hindi/Devanagari and Hinglish. DAX writes note text into Epic/Cerner/athena EHRs; MediKiosk must emit a validated NRCeS FHIR OPConsultRecord Bundle for ABDM. DAX has no pre-visit elicitation, no document digitization, and no ABDM role. Net effect: DAX strengthens MediKiosk's differentiation on every stated axis (offline, India residency, NRCeS-conformant emission, per-field provenance, physician attestation, bilingual). The one genuine threat is trajectory, not current overlap - Microsoft's HIMSS 2026 multilingual expansion (58 languages, including Hindi) and global region growth show the language moat is time-limited, though there is still no India region, no offline mode, and no ABDM/NRCeS conformance.

business_info.license: Proprietary, closed-source commercial software; no open license.
business_info.pricing: No public self-serve price. Historically quoted at roughly $369-$830 per provider per month plus a one-time $650-$700 setup/implementation fee, with some systems citing $8,000-$10,000 per clinician per year all-in. Microsoft published a reduced Dragon Copilot list price on 1 May 2026, and authorized resellers now advertise about $159.99 per user per month on a 12-month term plus setup and annual maintenance [uncertain - reseller-sourced]. Enterprise volume discounts apply.
business_info.funding: No venture funding of its own; Microsoft acquired Nuance Communications for approximately $19.7 billion (announced 2021, closed 2022), and DAX/Dragon Copilot is funded inside Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare.
business_info.commercial_status: Commercial enterprise product sold directly by Microsoft and through authorized resellers; production at scale in US and select European markets.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Abridge, Ambience Healthcare, Suki, Nabla, DeepScribe, Freed, Commure Scribe and other ambient scribes. Abridge and Ambience are cited as winning marquee health-system deals on features DAX was slower to ship (inline AI editing, coding depth), and Microsoft's May 2026 price cut is widely read as a response to Abridge, Ambience and Suki.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Epic (Hyperdrive, Haiku, Canto; native bidirectional write-back), Oracle Health/Cerner, athenahealth, MEDITECH, plus 200+ EHRs via the Dragon Medical One footprint. Azure Health Data Services (HL7 FHIR R4, DICOMweb) and Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare; Microsoft 365 Copilot Work IQ; partner AI apps/agents via Microsoft Marketplace (Canary Speech, Humata Health, Optum, Regard). No ABDM gateway role (HIP/HIU/PHR), no Health Locker integration.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: Microsoft is consolidating Dragon Copilot as the anchor of an enterprise healthcare AI ecosystem (BAA-covered Azure, Sentinal audit, Purview governance, Partner marketplace). It has global expansion into US, Canada, UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Austria, Belgium, Netherlands and Switzerland, but no India availability or India data-residency option. Procurement is enterprise-gated and exposed to competitive price pressure; the overall ambient-scribe category is crowding and price-compressing.

history.release_date: DAX (Dragon Ambient eXperience) launched by Nuance in 2020; Nuance acquired by Microsoft in 2022; DAX Copilot became fully embedded in Epic in 2023. [uncertain - exact launch month]
key_milestones: 2021-2022 - Microsoft announces and closes the ~$19.7B acquisition of Nuance.
2023 - DAX Copilot becomes fully embedded in Epic; Atrium Health is the first health system to deploy it.
June 2023-Aug 2023 - NEJM AI Atrium Health longitudinal study and JAMA Network Open nonrandomized trial enroll.
March 2025 - Microsoft merges DAX Copilot with Dragon Medical One under the unified Dragon Copilot brand; Android/macOS/Windows/web added.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: (1) HIMSS 2026, 5 March 2026 - Microsoft positions Dragon Copilot as a unified AI clinical assistant with role-based experiences for physicians/nurses/radiologists, Microsoft 365 Copilot 'Work IQ' context, partner AI apps/agents, and multilingual conversation capture in 58 languages automatically converted to the primary language of each country; availability listed for US, Canada, UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Austria, Belgium, Netherlands, Switzerland. (2) Dragon Copilot 3.6 release notes - diagnosis-aware notes using ambient recording for Assessment & Plan; Epic FHIR API activation for AllergyIntolerance, Binary, DocumentReference, Location, MedicationDispense, MedicationRequest and PractitionerRole (all R4); SMART App Launch 2.x / FHIR R4 for desktop EHR embedding. (3) 1 May 2026 - Microsoft publishes a reduced Dragon Copilot list price (resellers around $159.99/user/month), read as a response to Abridge/Ambience/Suki. (4) 21 August 2026 - General Availability of Dragon Copilot AI Apps and Agents for physician workflows through Microsoft Marketplace, with self-service partner onboarding, validation and certification. (5) Radiology experience enters preview in the US.

market_positioning.target_users: Physicians, nurses and radiologists inside large US and European health systems, plus clinical documentation and revenue-cycle teams; not solo or small practices.
market_positioning.market_segment: Ambient clinical documentation / clinical workflow AI (during-encounter scribing, not pre-visit intake or FHIR document tooling).
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Marketed as a unified 'AI clinical assistant' that streamlines documentation, surfaces critical information and automates routine tasks across role-based experiences, integrated with EHRs and extensible via a governed marketplace - with enterprise-grade security and compliance (HIPAA BAA, HITRUST CSF, SOC 2 Type II). The commercial pitch is 'unify, simplify, scale' clinical AI on Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare.
